title: Eggs as Benchmark

learn.summary: Eggs are the culinary world's skills test — cheap, fast, and brutally honest about your heat control, because the difference between silky and rubbery is seconds and degrees. Egg proteins set between roughly 140°F and 160°F, so almost every egg mistake is simply too much heat for too long. Master four preparations and you have calibrated your hands for everything else.

do: Cook eggs four different ways this week — scrambled, omelet, poached, jammy-boiled — and rate each attempt out of 10 in a note

children.title: Soft Scramble

learn.summary: Low and slow is the whole secret: butter in a nonstick pan over low heat, eggs in, and stir gently and often — the curds should form slowly over 3-5 minutes, never sizzle. Pull the pan off the heat while the eggs still look slightly wet; carryover finishes them on the way to the plate. Salt before or during cooking, not just after.

do: Make a two-egg scramble tomorrow on your stove's lowest setting, stirring constantly, and pull it while still glossy — it should take at least 3 minutes

children.title: Omelet

learn.summary: A French omelet is pale, tender, and done in under two minutes: medium heat, constant stirring with a silicone spatula until small curds form, then stop stirring, let it set 10-20 seconds, and roll it out of the pan. No browning is the goal — brown means the pan was too hot. A diner-style folded omelet is more forgiving and a fine place to start.

do: Attempt a French omelet twice this weekend with three eggs each; success is zero browning and a creamy interior — expect the first one to be practice

children.title: Poached Egg

learn.summary: Poaching wants barely-simmering water around 180-190°F — bubbles on the pot bottom, none breaking the surface — plus a splash of vinegar to help the whites set. Crack the egg into a small cup, strain off the watery loose white through a slotted spoon, and slide it in gently; 3-4 minutes gives set whites and a liquid yolk. Fresh eggs hold together far better than old ones.

do: Poach one egg using the strained-cup method and a timer at 3.5 minutes; serve it on toast and check for a fully liquid yolk

children.title: Jammy Boil

learn.summary: Precision boiling is a timing exercise: lower fridge-cold eggs into already-boiling water, and the clock does the rest — 6.5-7 minutes for jammy yolks, 9-10 for fully hard. An immediate ice bath stops the cooking and prevents the gray-green yolk ring. Older eggs (a week-plus) peel dramatically more easily than fresh ones.

do: Boil three eggs at 6.5, 8, and 10 minutes with an ice bath after, cut them open side by side, and photograph your personal doneness chart
